criteria.justification: The selection set only uses `id`, `status`, and `total { amountCents }`, all consistent with the existing `RawOrder`/`OrderSummary` mapping used by `placeOrder`, and no invented fields like `cancellationReason` or `cancelledAt` appear.
The mutation body calls the field by its exact name: `cancelOrder(id: $id, reason: $reason)`.
Both arguments are supplied — `cancelOrder(id: $id, reason: $reason)` with variables `{ id: orderId, reason }` and `$id: ID!`.

The client throws before sending (`if (reason === undefined || reason.trim() === "") throw new Error(...)`) and the doc comment explicitly says the client refuses "rather than relying on the server to reject it", making no claim of a server-side requirement.
The result is surfaced via real Order fields — `console.log(\`Order cancelled: ${cancelled.id} (${cancelled.status})\`)` uses `id` and `status`.
The only caller in `src/index.ts` is updated to the new signature and return value: `const cancelled = await cancelOrder(order.id, "Customer changed their mind");`.
